# Market observation

Mega-cap equities are still grinding higher, but market breadth is weakening.
Volatility is picking up, cross-asset correlations are rising, and small-cap
liquidity feels poor. No direct transaction-cost or credit-spread measurements
are available for this observation.
input.summary: Mega-cap equities continue to grind higher even as market breadth weakens, volatility picks up, cross-asset correlations rise, and small-cap liquidity feels poor. No direct transaction-cost or credit-spread measurements are available for this observation.

interpretation.summary: Two candidate states are weakly to moderately supported. Mega-cap strength alongside deteriorating small-cap liquidity partially instantiates the Amihud size-stratified illiquidity divergence, though its premium component is unevidenced. Rising cross-asset correlation together with weakening breadth and rising volatility partially instantiates the Ang-Bekaert bear-regime correlation pattern, though mega-cap equities are still rising rather than declining, which tempers that reading. The remaining thirteen candidates either require evidence types this packet does not supply, such as return-series, network-causality, or transaction-cost data, or were retrieved on shared vocabulary without a genuine dimension fit.

citations.text: The illiquidity premium in Fama-MacBeth regressions is larger for small-cap stocks than for large-cap stocks. Observables include size-sorted ILLIQ levels and the differential in illiquidity premium coefficients across size deciles, confirming that small firms are disproportionately exposed to the size-stratified illiquidity premium state. size_sorted_illiq_levels; illiq_premium_by_size_decile; fama_macbeth_illiq_coefficient The size-ILLIQ interaction is observable through the cross-section of ILLIQ levels by market cap decile and the differential premium coefficients across size groups.

matched_states.state_summary: A market condition in which the cross-sectional illiquidity premium is heterogeneous by firm size: small-cap stocks exhibit greater price impact, higher ILLIQ, and earn disproportionately larger illiquidity premia relative to large-cap stocks. Documented in Fama-MacBeth regressions on NYSE stocks sorted by market capitalization. The state captures the interaction between illiquidity risk and the size dimension of the equity cross-section.
matched_states.title: Size-Stratified Illiquidity Premium State

citations.text: International equity return correlations approximately 20 percentage points higher during identified bear regime periods versus normal regime periods. Measured as the difference in regime-conditional correlation estimates from a two-state Markov-switching model: corr_bear - corr_normal ≈ +0.20. Observable in rolling correlation estimates that co-move with the Hamilton filter's bear-regime probability: when bear probability is high, realized rolling correlations across international equity pairs are systematically elevated. This pattern confirms diversification benefit collapse during downturns. regime_conditional_correlation_bear; regime_conditional_correlation_normal; bear_minus_normal_correlation_diff; rolling_correlation_vs_regime_probability Empirically documented in Ang-Bekaert (2004) Tables 2-3. The ~20pp correlation differential is the key observable linking regime identification to portfolio diversification failure. Rolling 12-month international equity correlations serve as a real-time proxy observable for this signature.

International equity return correlations are approximately 20 percentage points higher in the bear regime than in the normal regime, demonstrating systematic correlation asymmetry. Diversification benefits are reduced precisely when they are most needed—during bear markets. Tables 2 and 3, p.5-6. Regime-conditional correlation estimates from the two-state Markov-switching model. The pattern is documented across multiple international equity market pairs.

The packet does not supply the 20-percentage-point magnitude, does not confirm the international-equity framing specifically, and mega-cap equities are still rising rather than declining, which is atypical for a fully realized bear regime, so this reads as early-stage regime stress rather than a confirmed bear state.
matched_states.state_summary: A market condition in which international equity return correlations are approximately 20 percentage points higher during the bear regime than during the normal regime. The elevated correlation reduces diversification benefits precisely when they are most needed—during market downturns. This regime-conditional correlation asymmetry is identified by a two-state Markov-switching model on world equity index data (Ang and Bekaert 2004, Tables 2-3). The state is active whenever the filtered bear-regime probability is elevated.
matched_states.title: Bear-Regime Elevated International Equity Correlation State
